The Institute of Physics Henry Moseley Medal and Prize is named after him, with memorial plaques at Manchester and Eton; Robert Millikan wrote that the war's 'snuffing out of this young life' was itself a grave loss.

name: Ignaz Semmelweis, 1847–1865

presentEffect.text: Handwashing is recognised as the antiseptic policy he pioneered, and Google marked 20 March 2020 with a Doodle to promote it during the COVID-19 pandemic. The 'Semmelweis reflex' names the rejection of new knowledge that conflicts with entrenched norms; a Budapest medical university, a museum in his birth house and the Ignác Semmelweis Prize bear his name.

name: Gregor Mendel, 1865–1866

presentEffect.text: His experiments, begun in 1856 on some 28,000 plants, led to the laws of segregation and independent assortment, known as Mendelian inheritance. Hugo de Vries, Carl Correns and Erich von Tschermak independently confirmed them in 1900, launching modern genetics, and the genes behind his seven traits were identified by 2025.

presentEffect.text: His 'lost notebook' was rediscovered in 1976 by George Andrews, and the Ramanujan conjecture on the tau function was proven in 1973 as a consequence of Pierre Deligne's work.
